skills.name: kstack/airgap-verify
skills.description: Run the air-gap compliance audit and enforce zero unauthorized cloud egress before classified or private workloads execute.

outputs.checks: Per-check results with severity and detail
outputs.attestation_sha256: Sealed attestation hash of the audit record

skills.instructions:
# KStack Air-Gap Verify Skill (Compliance Auditor Role)

## Overview
Executes the `/v1/airgap/audit` boundary check: loopback socket inventory, environment egress surface, and per-check verdicts that gate whether classified payloads may run at all.

## Execution Rules
1. When the audit is unavailable or fails, the verdict is UNVERIFIED — treat as non-compliant and block egress-dependent work. Never infer compliance from a prior pass.
2. Any request flagged `private`, `air_gap`, or classified must not proceed to a cloud model until a current COMPLIANT verdict exists.
3. The audit record is append-only evidence: expose the attestation hash verbatim, never paraphrase or regenerate it.
4. Report per-check results honestly, including skipped or failed checks — a partial audit is not a passing audit.

inputs.tool_name: Tool the grant covers (edit_file, write_file, run_command)
inputs.scope: Exact command or relative path glob the grant is limited to
inputs.model_id: Model the grant is bound to
inputs.prompt_version: Prompt version the grant is bound to

skills.instructions:
# KStack Approval Grant Skill (Policy Admin Role)

## Overview
Manages durable standing approvals via `/v1/approval-rules`. A grant is persisted policy — it survives restarts, is recorded in `.keelway/approval_rules.json`, and is enforced at runtime by exact tool and scope match.

## Execution Rules
1. Scopes must be explicit and safe: unscoped grants and patterns reaching `.keelway`, `.kora`, or `.git` are rejected by the store — do not attempt to work around the rejection.
2. Every grant binds to the granting model and prompt version. When either drifts, the rule pauses; reconfirm via `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/reconfirm` rather than recreating it.
3. Revocation is durable (`DELETE /v1/approval-rules/{id}`) and takes effect at the next runtime match — a revoked rule must cause the action to return to the approval queue.
4. List state reflects the store only. Never present a locally assumed or cached rule as granted when the API is unreachable.
5. All create, reconfirm, and revoke operations carry an audit event; unauthorized principals must receive the denial, not a silent no-op.

outputs.savings_usd: Quantified open-weight savings versus cloud spend

skills.instructions:
# KStack Cost Ledger Skill (Economics Auditor Role)

## Overview
Reads `/v1/usage` — the aggregate economics report over the cost ledger: billed cloud expenditure, entries recorded, per-model accounting, and the quantified savings of open-weight inference over cloud models.

## Execution Rules
1. Figures come from the ledger verbatim — cost is an audit surface, not a marketing claim.
2. `entries_recorded` of zero means no measured spend; report it as such rather than implying free operation.
3. Distinguish billed external expenditure from local $0.00 OpenCore spend — conflating the two fabricates savings.
4. The ledger is append-only evidence; a gap in coverage is disclosed, not interpolated.

skills.name: kstack/finops-forecast

inputs.projected_tokens: Optional forward token volume to price

outputs.savings_usd: Quantified delta between the two paths
outputs.projection: Forward cost estimate at the projected volume

skills.instructions:
# KStack FinOps Forecast Skill (FinOps Analyst Role)

## Overview
Reads `/v1/usage` economics — total billed cloud expenditure, entries recorded, and per-model cost accounting — plus the quota/pricing simulator to quantify the savings of OpenCore local inference versus BYOM external API spend, and to project forward cost at a given token volume.

## Execution Rules
1. Report ledger figures verbatim — billed expenditure and entry counts come from the cost ledger, never estimated.
2. When usage data is empty or the ledger is unavailable, report spend as unmeasured — never fabricate a savings figure.
3. Paid-tier token markup is 0% — a projection that assumes markup contradicts the published commercial model and must not be emitted.
4. Local inference is costed honestly: $0.00 vendor spend is real for OpenCore weights, but note hardware amortization is out of ledger scope.

skills.name: kstack/flight-tape-verify
skills.description: Verify Merkle hash-chain integrity of flight recorder tapes and produce sealed verification receipts for agent executions.

inputs.trace_id: Optional specific tape segment to verify; omitted verifies the full chain

outputs.first_bad_seq: Sequence index of the first integrity break when invalid

skills.instructions:
# KStack Flight-Tape Verify Skill (Auditor Role)

## Overview
Verifies the append-only Merkle chain backing the flight recorder via `/v1/audit/verify`, and fetches Merkle proofs for individual entries. Any truncation or mutation breaks verification — that break is the finding.

## Execution Rules
1. Verification failure is a security finding, not an error to retry: report the first bad sequence verbatim and stop.
2. Secrets, tokens, and private key material must never appear in skill output, even when present in tape records — surface redacted forms only.
3. A verification receipt is evidence of what was checked at a point in time; include chain length and timestamp so the receipt cannot be replayed as proof of a different chain.
4. If the tape store is unreachable, report UNVERIFIED rather than claiming the chain is valid.

skills.name: kstack/golden-eval
skills.description: Run the golden evaluation benchmark, seal evaluation receipts, and compare drift between candidate and reference runs.

inputs.compare_to: Optional prior receipt or model to drift-compare against

outputs.pass_at_1: Pass@1 rate across the benchmark tasks
outputs.drift: Drift comparison outcome when a reference is supplied

skills.instructions:
# KStack Golden Eval Skill (Eval Engineer Role)

## Overview
Executes `/v1/evals/run` — the golden benchmark producing a cryptographic `EvaluationReceipt` — reads `/v1/evals/history` for prior receipts, and uses `/v1/evals/drift/compare` to measure drift between a candidate and a reference run.

## Execution Rules
1. A regression gate reads the sealed receipt, not a verbal summary — quote `pass_at_1` and the receipt id verbatim.
2. `save_receipt=false` produces an unsealed estimate; label it as such and never promote it to a gate input.
3. Drift comparison is evidence, not verdict: report the measured delta and the gate threshold side by side.
4. On evaluator unavailability the run is UNMEASURED — do not carry a prior pass forward as proof.

skills.name: kstack/investigate
skills.description: Systematic root-cause debugging, error trace capture, and minimal defect reproduction without speculative edits.

inputs.failing_test: Optional failing test command or file

outputs.reproduced: Boolean indicator if defect was confirmed
outputs.affected_components: List of culpable file paths and symbols
outputs.minimal_repro: Minimal reproducer script or test command

skills.instructions:
# KStack Investigate Skill (Debugger Role)

## Overview
Performs systematic root-cause diagnosis of defects, test failures, and unexpected behaviors. Never propose mutations before reproducing the failure.

## Investigation Discipline
1. Reproduce with the smallest relevant test or script before touching code.
2. Distinguish product defect, invalid test expectation, and environment failure.
3. Inspect stack traces, variable values, and error output inside the verified sandbox.
4. Formulate the minimal repair plan with explicit verification assertions.
4. Prefer flight-tape replay and sealed trace inspection over speculative re-execution — the recorded run is the ground truth.
5. When a reproduction requires a Tier-3 action (network egress, push, deploy), record the need and stop for approval rather than executing it.
6. Preserve Merkle-chain evidence: never truncate or rewrite tape records to make a reproduction cleaner.

skills.name: kstack/kbrain-fact
skills.description: Record and query scope-governed KBrain memory facts with ACL boundaries and secret-leakage protection.

inputs.scope: agent, project, or org ACL scope

outputs.matched: Matching facts returned on query operations

skills.instructions:
# KStack KBrain Fact Skill (Knowledge Curator Role)

## Overview
Records and queries workspace knowledge via `/v1/kbrain/fact` and `/v1/kbrain/facts` — scope-governed facts enforced by an ACL boundary (agent ≤ project ≤ org) with pre-storage DLP secret blocking and P-10 conflict resolution.

## Execution Rules
1. A `SecretLeakDetectedError` (HTTP 422) is a hard stop — never retry the same statement with secrets merely obfuscated.
2. Facts are scope-governed: a caller may only read facts at or below its max scope, and write at its declared scope. Do not report facts beyond the caller's boundary.
3. A conflicting fact requires P-10 resolution — surface the conflict, never silently overwrite.
4. Record provenance (`provenance_uri`, `provenance_reason`) on every fact; a fact without provenance is weaker evidence.

skills.name: kstack/kflow-orchestrate
skills.description: Execute KFlow DAG workflows and multi-agent team plans, returning sealed proof packets for every run.

inputs.goal: Natural-language objective to plan or execute
inputs.workflow_id: Optional registered KFlow workflow to run directly

outputs.run_id: Execution run identifier recorded on the flight tape
outputs.nodes_executed: Count of DAG nodes that ran to completion
outputs.proof_packet_sha256: Sealed proof packet hash attesting to the run

skills.instructions:
# KStack KFlow Orchestrate Skill (Orchestrator Role)

## Overview
Drives the KFlow execution engine — `/v1/orchestration/team/plan` decomposes a goal into a role-specialized agent DAG, and `/execute` runs it through the governed pipeline with per-node approvals and sealed proof output.

## Execution Rules
1. Every run must produce a sealed proof packet; a run that cannot seal is reported as unverified, not successful.
2. Long-running executions (multi-minute node work, real test suites) are normal — poll to completion rather than declaring a timeout failure early.
3. Node-level gates still apply: a DAG may pause for P-10 approval mid-run, and that pause is expected orchestration behavior, not a stall.
4. Multi-agent plans never bypass individual human approval — role-specialized nodes inherit the principal's permission envelope.
5. Schedule state is process-scoped; represent intervals and run counts as live registry state, not durable history.

skills.name: kstack/mesh-verify

outputs.delegation: Delegation outcome and proof reference for delegate actions
outputs.pruned: Stale peers removed for prune actions

skills.instructions:
# KStack Mesh Verify Skill (Mesh Operator Role)

## Overview
Operates the `/v1/mesh/*` surface: `/v1/mesh/status` and `/v1/mesh/peers` for fleet visibility, `/v1/mesh/delegate` for peer execution, `/v1/mesh/heartbeat` for liveness, and `/v1/mesh/prune` for stale-peer eviction.

## Execution Rules
1. Delegation is a governance event — carry the delegation proof reference back verbatim.
2. A peer missing heartbeats is stale evidence, not dead capacity: report last-seen state honestly before pruning.
3. Prune is destructive within the mesh view — confirm the peer is actually stale per the heartbeat window first.
4. Never represent a locally simulated mesh as real remote peers; state the boundary when the mesh runs in simulation.

skills.name: kstack/modernize
skills.description: Dependency upgrade analysis, deprecated API call site detection, and safe migration path planning.

inputs.target_version: Desired version constraint or semver tag

outputs.breaking_changes: List of breaking syntax or behavior modifications
outputs.deprecated_apis: List of culpable call sites in the repository
outputs.migration_steps: Ordered steps to update imports and invocations

skills.instructions:
# KStack Modernize Skill (Engineer Role)

## Overview
Analyzes package and library dependencies, identifies deprecated AST call sites across the codebase, and drafts an atomic migration path.

## Workflow
1. Inspect `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, or requirements files for current pinned version.
2. Analyze AST call sites and import statements using the target library.
3. Compare against target version breaking changes and deprecations.
4. Draft the minimal, backward-compatible migration plan adhering to `outputs`.
4. Migration plans must preserve durable state: approval rules, governance policy, flight tapes, and vault records survive dependency changes.
5. Version drift that invalidates model/prompt-bound approval rules must trigger reconfirm steps in the migration plan.

skills.name: kstack/p10-gate
skills.description: Evaluate and record P-10 human approval decisions for Tier-3 agent actions through the governed approval endpoint with sealed receipts.

inputs.task_id: Identifier of the pending gated task awaiting human decision
inputs.decision: approve, deny, or allow_always grant scope

outputs.receipt_id: Sealed approval receipt identifier recorded on the flight tape
outputs.rule_id: Standing approval rule id when allow_always persisted a rule
outputs.decision_recorded: Boolean confirming the decision reached the ledger

skills.instructions:
# KStack P-10 Gate Skill (Gatekeeper Role)

## Overview
Routes Tier-3 (high-risk) agent actions through the human approval gate. A P-10 decision is a governance event: it is recorded on the Merkle flight tape, produces a sealed receipt, and — when scoped — persists a standing approval rule bound to the granting model and prompt version.

## Execution Rules
1. Never auto-approve. The skill may only carry a human's explicit decision to the gate; it cannot manufacture one.
2. A missing, revoked, or model/prompt-mismatched standing rule must resolve to "requires approval" — fail closed, never fail open.
3. `allow_always` persists via `POST /v1/approval-rules` and binds the rule to the current `model_id` and `prompt_version`; drift pauses the rule until reconfirm.
4. Every decision emits an audit event and returns its receipt. If the API rejects the decision (RBAC, unsafe scope), surface the denial — do not retry as a different principal.
5. On API unavailability, report the action as still pending. Never represent an unrecorded decision as granted.

skills.name: kstack/plan
skills.description: Architectural decomposition, file path planning, and risk blast radius estimation.
skills.instructions:
# KStack Plan Skill (Architect Role)

## Overview
Decomposes an engineering objective into minimal, deterministic file-level steps without applying mutations.

## Workflow
1. Read the target workspace and examine symbols and imports related to `goal`.
2. Formulate ordered steps: target path, purpose, constraints, and test commands.
3. Compute blast radius based on import graph depth and shared library touched.
4. Output structured plan JSON adhering to `outputs`.
4. Plans must declare the autonomy tier each step requires and which steps need P-10 human approval before they may execute.
5. A plan that requires cloud egress for classified or private payloads must route those steps to local open-weight models or mark them blocked — plans respect the air-gap invariant.
6. Steps that mutate the workspace must name their isolation boundary (worktree + checkpoint) before execution begins.

skills.name: kstack/qa

inputs.test_command: Command line string for test runner

skills.instructions:
# KStack QA Skill (QA Lead Role)

## Overview
Executes test suites within restricted workspace sandboxes, captures exit status, and certifies reproduction or resolution.

## Execution Rules
1. Never invoke network egress unless explicitly configured.
2. Terminate immediately upon test failure when in fail-fast mode.
3. Record duration, exit code, and test stdout in sealed execution proof.
4. Test output and failure traces may enter the flight tape; secrets and credentials in output must be flagged, never reproduced.
5. A run that leaves the workspace dirty must report the residue; silent cleanup hides state the next run will inherit.

skills.name: kstack/repomap-sync

outputs.repo_map: Condensed AST symbol map for prompt augmentation
outputs.total_files: Count of scanned and indexed files
outputs.symbols_indexed: Count of extracted class, function, and method symbols

skills.instructions:
# KStack RepoMap Sync Skill (General Role)

## Overview
Maintains an up-to-date semantic symbol index and condensed repository map using pure-Python AST parsing and deterministic vector projection.

## Execution Rules
1. Never invoke external network sockets or third-party embeddings services.
2. Scrub all credentials and tokens from scanned documentation and source comments before storing in KBrain.
3. Cache symbol digests incrementally to minimize re-indexing latency.
3. Extracted symbols and call hierarchies sync to KBrain only — no extracted repository content leaves the local boundary.
4. Sync records the workspace and index version so stale maps cannot be mistaken for current state.

skills.name: kstack/review
skills.description: AST diff analysis, secret leakage detection, and gate integrity auditing.

outputs.findings: List of security or logic warnings

skills.instructions:
# KStack Review Skill (Reviewer Role)

## Overview
Inspects proposed unified diffs for security regressions, accidental secret commits, syntax breakage, and policy compliance.

## Verification Gates
1. Secret Scan: Assert no tokens, keys, passwords, or credentials appear in additions.
2. Scope Check: Verify all touched files reside strictly within permitted workspace boundaries.
3. Gate Integrity: Confirm all elevated actions obtained human quorum or approval.
4. Fail-Closed Invariants: verify air-gap classification, secret redaction in tapes/errors, sandboxed execution, and append-only audit writes were not weakened.
5. Standing approval rules are policy: diffs that widen rule scope, remove model/prompt binding, or skip the runtime match are security regressions, not refactors.

skills.name: kstack/sbom-audit
skills.description: Generate and inspect the CycloneDX SBOM for dependency inventory, license posture, and supply-chain evidence.
skills.instructions:
# KStack SBOM Audit Skill (Supply-Chain Auditor Role)

## Overview
Reads `/v1/sbom` — the CycloneDX software bill of materials — to enumerate runtime dependencies, license posture, and supply-chain evidence for release qualification and compliance review.

## Execution Rules
1. The SBOM is generated from the live environment; a stale export is not evidence of current posture.
2. Report `component_count` and license distribution verbatim — a dependency omitted from the count is a finding, not noise.
3. An unknown or unmapped license is flagged, never guessed.
4. SBOM inspection is read-only evidence gathering; vulnerability verdicts belong to the scanner skill, not this one.

skills.name: kstack/schedule-ops

inputs.spec: Schedule definition for create (trigger, cadence, target workflow)

skills.instructions:
# KStack Schedule Ops Skill (Automation Operator Role)

## Overview
Operates `/v1/schedules` — listing registered cron and webhook triggers and creating new schedules bound to governed workflow executions.

## Execution Rules
1. A schedule that mutates workspace state runs under the same P-10 policy as a manual run — automation does not bypass the gate.
2. Webhook triggers are an egress surface; creating one against an unverified endpoint is a finding, not a convenience.
3. Report the persisted `schedule_id` verbatim on create; an unacknowledged create is reported as unconfirmed.
4. Inventory reads reflect the live registry — never answer from a cached list when asked for current schedules.

skills.name: kstack/security
skills.description: STRIDE threat modeling, NIST SP 800-53 SC-7 air-gap auditing, and SCA vulnerability scanning.

inputs.manifest_path: Path to project manifest or code tree

skills.instructions:
# KStack Security Skill (Security Lead Role)

## Overview
Evaluates the repository against NIST SP 800-53 SC-7 boundaries, STRIDE threat categories, and software supply chain components.

## Audit Checks
1. Zero egress socket verification.
2. Malicious package script inspection.
3. Trust boundary and permission escalation detection.
4. Air-gap and privacy classification are fail-closed: absence of an explicit COMPLIANT audit means non-compliant for gating purposes.
5. RBAC denials must name the required permission; a denial that does not name what was required is a finding.
6. Webhook, token, and quorum surfaces require positive verification — assert rejection of unsigned, replayed, and cross-role requests.

skills.name: kstack/ship
skills.description: Release qualification, test gate verification, signed flight tape sealing, and release receipt generation.

inputs.target_ref: Git commit or branch to qualify
inputs.required_gates: List of verification gates (unit, e2e, security, live_model)

outputs.passed_gates: List of successfully completed verification gates
outputs.flight_tape_sha256: Cryptographic hash of sealed flight tape

skills.instructions:
# KStack Ship Skill (Release Lead Role)

## Overview
Validates release readiness against fail-closed engineering gates, seals cryptographic flight tapes, and generates signed release receipts.

## Release Gates
1. Full test suite execution in verified OS sandbox.
2. Zero-secret and zero-leakage DLP audit across modified files.
3. Flight tape tamper detection and SHA-256 seal verification.
4. Gate integrity check: verify all mutating actions obtained human approval.
4. The manifest digest check, ruff, pytest, and frontend suites are gate requirements — a skipped gate is a release blocker, not a warning.
5. Every ship decision references the sealed execution proof; a release without a verifiable run record is not shippable.

skills.name: kstack/wcag-aa
skills.description: Enforce WCAG 2.2 AA on rendered surfaces — semantic landmarks, keyboard reachability, focus visibility, zero axe-core violations.

inputs.surface: Route or view identifier to audit (e.g. /app, a platform view id)

outputs.verdict: PASS or FAIL against the zero-violation gate
outputs.violations: axe-core violation list with rule ids and affected nodes
outputs.remediations: Ordered fix list when mode is remediate

skills.instructions:
# KStack WCAG AA Skill (Accessibility Auditor Role)

## Overview
Audits rendered surfaces for WCAG 2.2 AA conformance using the same axe-core gate the dev-app test suite enforces: semantic landmarks, name-role-value, keyboard reachability, focus visibility, live regions, and color contrast. Optionally produces a remediation list.

## Execution Rules
1. The gate is zero axe-core violations — one violation is a FAIL, never a warning.
2. Audit the rendered DOM, not source code; decorative text must not be flagged, and interactive elements must expose an accessible name.
3. Remediation must preserve existing accessible names and live-region behavior — shortening a visible label without updating `aria-label` regresses the contract.
4. Report violations with their axe rule id and node selector verbatim. Never paraphrase a violation into a pass.
5. RTL/bidirectional text and reduced-motion states are part of the audit surface, not optional extras.

skills.name: kstack/worktree-isolate
skills.description: Create isolated git worktrees and checkpoints so agent edits land in a disposable boundary with a real rollback path.

inputs.task_name: Slug identifying the agent task for branch and worktree naming

outputs.branch: Dedicated task branch for the agent's edits

skills.instructions:
# KStack Worktree Isolate Skill (Operator Role)

## Overview
Provisions the isolated execution boundary for agent edits: `POST /v1/worktrees` creates a detached worktree plus task branch, and `POST /v1/checkpoints` snapshots pre-edit state — including untracked files — so rollback is real, not aspirational.

## Execution Rules
1. Agent edits must land in the isolated worktree, never directly on the primary checkout. If isolation provisioning fails, do not begin edits.
2. Capture a checkpoint before the first agent mutation; report its id so the caller can restore via `POST /v1/checkpoints/{id}/restore`.
3. Worktree removal is restricted to agent-managed paths; never delete a worktree that contains uncommitted human changes without an explicit instruction.
4. If the workspace is not a git repository or worktree creation is denied, report the boundary as absent — do not simulate isolation by editing in place.
